The sun dipped low on the horizon, casting a golden hue over the overgrown garden, where wildflowers tangled with weeds, their colors vibrant against the backdrop of old stone walls. Mara knelt in the cool earth, her fingers digging into the soil, feeling the dampness seep into her skin. The earth smelled rich and alive, a sharp contrast to the faint tang of rust from the wrought-iron gate that creaked in the gentle breeze. She paused, brushing a lock of hair from her brow, its dampness sticking to her forehead.

“Are you going to bury yourself in there, or do you plan to actually plant something?” A voice broke through the stillness, teasing yet laced with a hint of genuine curiosity.

Mara glanced up to see Tom leaning against the gatepost, arms crossed over his chest, the late afternoon light catching the tousled strands of his hair. There was always something easy about his presence, as if he belonged there, as much as the garden itself. She offered a half-smile, pushing down the flutter of annoyance that rose at his lighthearted jab.

“Just trying to coax the life back into it,” she replied, her tone softer than she intended. “These flowers have a way of reminding you what was once here.”

Tom stepped closer, the crunch of gravel beneath his boots mingling with the whispering leaves. “Life has a funny way of coming back, doesn’t it?” His gaze drifted past her, taking in the tangled mass of petals and thorns. “Just like us, I guess.”

Mara felt a warmth rise in her chest, a mix of gratitude and something else—something unnameable that stirred beneath the surface.
